title: When Is a Numerological Search Finished? An Exhaustive Null to Depth 10, and a Depth Ceiling That Explains Why Deeper Cannot Help
description: WHAT WAS ATTEMPTED, PLAINLY. A modified-inertia gravity framework fixes its acceleration scale to the cosmological constant, a0 = cH_Lambda/Z with Z = sqrt(32pi/3) = 5.78881, and in doing so supplies exactly two dimensionless germs: the generation count 3 and the kernel germ sqrt(8pi/3). The attempt was to find out whether those same two germs also generate any dimensionless constant of the Standard Model -- that is, whether the coefficient that works for gravity extends to the mass and coupling sector. This was not a fishing expedition through arbitrary combinations of pi and small integers: a candidate expression was required to CONTAIN the germs (Gate B), which is what makes the search falsifiable rather than open-ended. Expressions were built by constructive enumeration -- a base leaf plus D-4 steps from a fixed 30-entry menu (leaf append with MUL/DIV, five power exponents, three unaries) -- so candidate count grows as 11 * 30^(D-4). Value-identical expressions were deduplicated at mpmath precision, so what is counted is DISTINCT VALUES, not distinct formulas. Every value was confronted with 19 measured dimensionless SM targets spanning eleven orders of magnitude in relative precision, from m_p/m_e at 1.7e-11 to the PMNS mixing angles at ~6e-2, through three gates: germ content, cross-sector interlock, and false-discovery control. THE ATTEMPT FAILED, EXHAUSTIVELY. 174,890,804 raw candidates enumerated; 42,534,139 distinct values; 82,613 in-window hits; ZERO surviving the gate; ZERO re-labelings. Depths 3 through 9 were already exhaustive clean nulls under the same machinery, so the range 3-10 is now PROVEN EMPTY rather than unexamined. Depth 10 is the first depth past 9 where the word exhaustive applies rather than sampled. THE INFORMATIVE RESULT IS NOT THE NULL BUT WHERE THE HITS LAND. Hit count is a monotone function of measurement-window width and of nothing else. The six most precisely measured targets in the set -- m_p/m_e, a_e, 1/alpha, m_n/m_p, m_mu/m_e, a_mu -- return EXACTLY ZERO hits across 42.5 million values. The loosely measured PMNS angles return 15,212 / 26,142 / 20,799. Every one of the 82,613 hits died in the FDR gate. This is what chance looks like drawn to scale, and it is a far more informative statement than 'we found nothing.' THE DEPTH CEILING. Formalising that observation: a constructive enumeration whose candidate count grows as B^(D-D0) exhausts any FIXED measurement precision w at a computable depth, D_max = D0 + ln(1/w)/ln(B), beyond which a single-target match is expected by chance and therefore carries no information however many digits it displays. For this vocabulary (B = 30, D0 = 4) the ceiling is D = 10.4 for 1/alpha and D = 13.1 for m_p/m_e, the most precisely measured ratio in physics. Two consequences. (a) DEEPER IS WORSE, NOT BETTER: each additional depth costs log2(B) = 4.9 bits of look-elsewhere for nothing while available target precision is fixed. Depth 18 costs 68.7 bits; the two most precisely measured numbers in physics supply 76.3 between them, which does not clear it. Our own depth-10-to-18 sampling campaign -- 1,059 passes, ~29,000 in-window hits, zero survivors -- was therefore incapable of establishing a single-target result BY CONSTRUCTION, a fact we did not appreciate until after running it. (b) DISCRIMINATING POWER MUST COME FROM SIMULTANEOUS MATCHING across independent sectors, with a threshold in bits, SUM_i log2(1/w_i) > log2(N(D)) + margin. Counting interlocked targets is the wrong statistic: three loosely measured targets carry 24.7 bits where two tight ones carry 76.3. WHY NOTHING WAS THERE -- FOUR STRUCTURAL OBSTRUCTIONS, each established separately and each standing without the search. (1) NUMBER FIELD: Z carries a transcendental sqrt(pi) while the flavour and coupling data are algebraic, so an exact identity requires the sqrt(pi) to cancel -- in which case the germ was not load-bearing. (2) PERIOD RING: half-integer versus integer weight, with the weight-1 slot empty, the two rings disjoint exactly where a bridge would have to live. (3) DICTIONARY/CATEGORY: u = a0/g is an acceleration RATIO while a renormalisation scale is an ENERGY; the only dimensional bridge, a0/2c with hbar and c, lands ~38 orders below the electron. (4) VARYING CONSTANTS, the one experimental closure: if any SM constant tracked the dark-energy density as strongly as a0 does, atomic clocks would have seen it -- the coupling is bounded to |p| <= 6e-8. METHOD: A HELD-BACK VALIDATION SET, AND WHY ONE OF THEM IS NEARLY WORTHLESS. A search that iterates until a gate passes is fitting to the gate, so two targets were excluded from every search pool: koide_Q_lep (tight) and r_tau_mu (loose). Reported against interest, the tight one is nearly worthless as a holdout -- measured koide_Q_lep = 0.666660511 +/- 6.8e-6 sits 0.91 sigma from exact 2/3, an answer known since Koide (1981), so a survivor landing on 2/3 passes while predicting nothing new. r_tau_mu has no famous closed form and is the stronger test despite being the looser one. Any holdout whose answer is already in the literature measures nothing. BUGS THE GUARDS CAUGHT, recorded because the guards are the reason the null is trustworthy. A merge that re-keyed float64 silently discarded 19% of depth 8's distinct values, caught by requiring the sharded path to reproduce committed serial counts EXACTLY before being pointed at new depth. Shard-local record indices made hit records disagree with the merged value array, caught by an existing REBUILD MISMATCH assertion. A holdout leak: two hard-coded target lists re-added koide_Q_lep by name after the dataset-level exclusion, so the search was briefly fitting a target documented as held back. And one in the opposite direction: applying the holdout filter unconditionally BROKE the replay gate, which must sweep the full historical target list to reproduce committed ground truth -- suppressing a guard to satisfy a methodological rule is its own failure mode. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. The look-elsewhere / multiple-comparisons argument is standard (Gross & Vitells 2010) and NOTHING HERE IS NEW STATISTICS; the contribution is its quantitative instantiation as a DEPTH ceiling for constructive-enumeration searches, plus a worked exhaustive null. The null is about one germ vocabulary at one depth under one gate -- not a statement about numerology in general. It says nothing about depth 11+ (~13.5 days sharded) or other germ vocabularies. Critically, IT NEITHER SUPPORTS NOR DAMAGES THE FRAMEWORK WHOSE GERMS IT USES: that framework's acceleration scale, the constant Z, the response sign and the gate frequency remain POSTULATED, NOT DERIVED, and this search does not bear on them. We also report an error of our own: the naive expected-count model N*2w OVERESTIMATES observed hits by ~100x because the value set clusters rather than distributing uniformly, so our own bits thresholds should be read as conservative rather than exact. HONEST SCALE. This is one increment on a wall that already had six supports, obtained at substantial engineering cost, in a search whose prior was low and remains low. Its value is that it CLOSES rather than leaves ajar: the range 3-10 is proven empty, and the ceiling says where examining further stops meaning anything. All numbers are printed by committed scripts at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula (project_atomos/).
notes: A NULL RESULT, PUBLISHED AS ONE. The search was an honest attempt to extend a gravity framework's forced germs (3 and sqrt(8pi/3)) into the Standard-Model parameter sector; it returned zero certified matches over an exhaustive depth-3-to-10 enumeration of 42.5 million distinct values against 19 targets. Published because (i) exhaustive nulls in this genre are almost never reported, so the space stays nominally open, and (ii) the hit distribution yields a reusable quantitative tool -- the depth ceiling D_max = D0 + ln(1/w)/ln(B) -- that tells any constructive-enumeration search in advance where single-target matching stops carrying information. Strict both-ways discipline: three implementation bugs caught by consistency guards, one methodological over-correction that broke a guard, one nearly-worthless holdout target, and a ~100x error in our own expected-count model are all reported in the paper rather than quietly fixed. The prior on this search was low and remains low. Explicitly disclaimed: no new statistics (the look-elsewhere argument is Gross & Vitells 2010), no statement about numerology in general, and no bearing either way on the framework whose germs were used. Reproducible from https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula
